To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
two Arabidopsis chloroplast-targeted Hsp70s are processed into similar-sized forms in chloroplasts and one of these forms can also be generated by stromal peptidase(s) in vitro.

the chloroplast-targeted Hsp70 proteins are processed into two or three forms in Arabidopsis, and that the processing of AtHsp 70-6 into a smaller-sized processed product occurs in a peptidase activity-independent manner.

two Arabidopsis HSP70 proteins are targeted to the stroma and are processed by the stromal peptidase and that one of the HSP70 proteins is processed to a smaller form by an unidentified peptidase in the absence of the organelle.
In summary, our research is concerned with
alternative processing of Hsp70 precursors during protein import into chloropastis.
the alternative processing of AtHsp7-6 and At-Hsp70-7 precursors during protein import into chloropast.
the alternative processing of Hsp70 precursors during protein import into chloroplas.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
AtHsp70s are imported into the chloroplasts and are processed into two different-sized mature forms by two different peptidases.
the AtHsp70 homolog of HSP70-IAP has yet to be identified.
Arabidopsis HSP70-6 and HSP70-7 are stromal proteins and are not related to HSP70-IAP.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the processing pathway for Arabidopsis chloroplast Hsp70s is more complex than that for the pea chloroplast Hsp60 homolog.
Arabidopsis has at least two chloroplast-targeted Hsp70 proteins (AtHsp-6 and 7) and that AtHsp70-I is a precursor protein for AtHsp70.
the precursor of AtHsp-70 was processed into three different mature forms and the larger two mature forms were localized in the stromal compartment of chloroplasts.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the processing of Hsp70-6 is different from that of the Hsp100 proteins.
the processing of the Arabidopsis Hsps is different from that of the pea Hsp70-Iap.
Arabidopsis has multiple Hsp70 homology proteins, some of which are processed in the chloroplasts in a manner that is different from that reported for Hsp70 in pea.
